hook.text: Your spouse needs a kidney. You'd donate but you're not a match. Another couple has the exact same problem—reversed.

buildup.text: Selling kidneys is illegal. But swapping donations is allowed: you give to their patient, they give to yours.

discovery.text: Al Roth built kidney exchange algorithms that find chains of compatible donors across dozens of hospitals nationwide.

twist.text: Altruistic donors start chains: one stranger's gift triggers a cascade that can save 10+ lives in a single chain.

climax.text: Roth shared the 2012 Nobel Prize. Kidney exchange saves thousands of lives yearly by redesigning who gives to whom.

punchline.text: The right swap saves a life no donation could.

quiz.question: How does kidney exchange work?
options: Algorithms match incompatible donor-patient pairs for swaps
